text:
Predicates:
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
BreedingBack(x) ::: x is a form of artificial selection by the deliberate selective breeding of domestic animals.
Resemble(x, y) ::: x resembles y.
Extinct(x) ::: x is extinct.
Premises:
∀x (BreedingBack(x) → ∀y (Animal(y) ∧ Resemble(x, y))) ::: Breeding back is a form of artificial selection by the deliberate selective breeding of domestic animals.
Animal(heckCattle) ∧ BreedingBack(heckCattle) ∧ Resemble(heckCattle, aurochs) ::: Heck cattle were bred-back in the 1920s to resemble the aurochs.
Animal(heckCattle) ::: Heck cattle are animals.
Animal(aurochs) ::: Aurochs are animals.
∃x (Animal(x) ∧ BreedingBack(x) ∧ ∃y (Animal(y) ∧ Extinct(y) ∧ Resemble(x, y))) ::: Some animals to be bred-back resemble animals that are extinct.
Conclusion:
Extinct(aurochs) ::: Aurochs are extinct.
